units.leftText: This is the burden that Habakkuk the prophet received in a vision:
units.rightText: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.

units.leftText: How long, O LORD, must I call for help but You do not hear, or cry out to You, “Violence!” but You do not save?
units.rightText: O Jehovah, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear? I cry out unto thee of violence, and thou wilt not save.

units.leftText: Why do You make me see iniquity? Why do You tolerate wrongdoing? Destruction and violence are before me. Strife is ongoing, and conflict abounds.
units.rightText: Why dost thou show me iniquity, and look upon perverseness? for destruction and violence are before me; and there is strife, and contention riseth up.

units.leftText: Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth. For the wicked hem in the righteous, so that justice is perverted. The LORD’s Answer
units.rightText: Therefore the law is slacked, and justice doth never go forth; for the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore justice goeth forth perverted.

units.leftText: “Look at the nations and observe— be utterly astounded! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe even if someone told you.
units.rightText: Behold ye among the nations, and look, and wonder marvellously; for I am working a work in your days, which ye will not believe though it be told you.
leftNotes: 1:5 LXX Look, you scoffers, wonder and perish!

units.leftText: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans — that ruthless and impetuous nation which marches through the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings not their own.
units.rightText: For, lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, that march through the breadth of the earth, to possess dwelling-places that are not theirs.

units.leftText: They are dreaded and feared; from themselves they derive justice and sovereignty.
units.rightText: They are terrible and dreadful; their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves.

units.leftText: Their horses are swifter than leopards, fiercer than wolves of the night. Their horsemen charge ahead, and their cavalry comes from afar. They fly like a vulture, swooping down to devour.
units.rightText: Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves; and their horsemen press proudly on: yea, their horsemen come from far; they fly as an eagle that hasteth to devour.

units.leftText: All of them come bent on violence; their hordes advance like the east wind; they gather prisoners like sand.
units.rightText: They come all of them for violence; the set of their faces is forwards; and they gather captives as the sand.

units.leftText: They scoff at kings and make rulers an object of scorn. They laugh at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it.
units.rightText: Yea, he scoffeth at kings, and princes are a derision unto him; he derideth every stronghold; for he heapeth up dust, and taketh it.

units.leftText: Then they sweep by like the wind and pass through. They are guilty; their own strength is their god.” Habakkuk’s Second Complaint (Psalm 11:1–7|PSA 11:1-7*)
units.rightText: Then shall he sweep by as a wind, and shall pass over, and be guilty, even he whose might is his god.

units.leftText: Are You not from everlasting, O LORD, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. O LORD, You have appointed them to execute judgment; O Rock, You have established them for correction.
units.rightText: Art not thou from everlasting, O Jehovah my God, my Holy One? we shall not die. O Jehovah, thou hast ordained him for judgment; and thou, O Rock, hast established him for correction.

units.leftText: Your eyes are too pure to look upon evil, and You cannot tolerate wrongdoing. So why do You tolerate the faithless? Why are You silent while the wicked swallow up those more righteous than themselves?
units.rightText: Thou that art of purer eyes than to behold evil, and that canst not look on perverseness, wherefore lookest thou upon them that deal treacherously, and holdest thy peace when the wicked swalloweth up the man that is more righteous than he;

units.leftText: You have made men like the fish of the sea, like creeping things that have no ruler.
units.rightText: and makest men as the fishes of the sea, as the creeping things, that have no ruler over them?

units.leftText: The foe pulls all of them up with a hook; he catches them in his dragnet, and gathers them in his fishing net; so he rejoices gladly.
units.rightText: He taketh up all of them with the angle, he catcheth them in his net, and gathereth them in his drag: therefore he rejoiceth and is glad.
leftNotes: 1:15 Literally He pulls all of them up

units.leftText: Therefore he sacrifices to his dragnet and burns incense to his fishing net, for by these things his portion is sumptuous and his food is rich.
units.rightText: Therefore he sacrificeth unto his net, and burneth incense unto his drag; because by them his portion is fat, and his food plenteous.

units.leftText: Will he, therefore, empty his net and continue to slay nations without mercy?
units.rightText: Shall he therefore empty his net, and spare not to slay the nations continually?

units.leftText: I will stand at my guard post and station myself on the ramparts. I will watch to see what He will say to me, and how I should answer when corrected.
units.rightText: I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will look forth to see what he will speak with me, and what I shall answer concerning my complaint.

units.leftText: Then the LORD answered me: “Write down this vision and clearly inscribe it on tablets, so that a herald may run with it.
units.rightText: And Jehovah answered me, and said, Write the vision, and make it plain upon tablets, that he may run that readeth it.

units.leftText: For the vision awaits an appointed time; it testifies of the end and does not lie. Though it lingers, wait for it, since it will surely come and will not delay.
units.rightText: For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hasteth toward the end, and shall not lie: though it tarry, wait for it; because it will surely come, it will not delay.
leftNotes: 2:3 Or Though He lingers, wait for Him, since He will surely come and will not delay; see also LXX; cited in Hebrews 10:37|HEB 10:37*.

units.leftText: Look at the proud one; his soul is not upright — but the righteous will live by faith —
units.rightText: Behold, his soul is puffed up, it is not upright in him; but the righteous shall live by his faith.
leftNotes: 2:4 LXX If he should draw back, My soul has no pleasure in him
2:4 Or faithfulness; cited in Romans 1:17|ROM 1:17*, Galatians 3:11, and Hebrews 10:38

units.leftText: and wealth indeed betrays him. He is an arrogant man never at rest. He enlarges his appetite like Sheol, and like Death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations to himself and collects all the peoples as his own. Woe to the Chaldeans
units.rightText: Yea, moreover, wine is treacherous, a haughty man, that keepeth not at home; who enlargeth his desire as Sheol, and he is as death, and cannot be satisfied, but gathereth unto him all nations, and heapeth unto him all peoples.

units.leftText: Will not all of these take up a taunt against him, speaking with mockery and derision: ‘Woe to him who amasses what is not his and makes himself rich with many loans! How long will this go on?’
units.rightText: Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and that ladeth himself with pledges!

units.leftText: Will not your creditors suddenly arise and those who disturb you awaken? Then you will become their prey.
units.rightText: Shall they not rise up suddenly that shall bite thee, and awake that shall vex thee, and thou shalt be for booty unto them?

units.leftText: Because you have plundered many nations, the remnant of the people will plunder you— because of your bloodshed against man and your violence against the land, the city, and all their dwellers.
units.rightText: Because thou hast plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples shall plunder thee, because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all that dwell therein.

units.leftText: Woe to him who builds his house by unjust gain, to place his nest on high and escape the hand of disaster!
units.rightText: Woe to him that getteth an evil gain for his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the hand of evil!

units.leftText: You have plotted shame for your house by cutting off many peoples and forfeiting your life.
units.rightText: Thou hast devised shame to thy house, by cutting off many peoples, and hast sinned against thy soul.

units.leftText: For the stones will cry out from the wall, and the rafters will echo it from the woodwork.
units.rightText: For the stone shall cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the timber shall answer it.

units.leftText: Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and establishes a town by iniquity!
units.rightText: Woe to him that buildeth a town with blood, and establisheth a city by iniquity!

units.leftText: Is it not indeed from the LORD of Hosts that the labor of the people only feeds the fire, and the nations weary themselves in vain?
units.rightText: Behold, is it not of Jehovah of hosts that the peoples labor for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for vanity?

units.leftText: For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD as the waters cover the sea.
units.rightText: For the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Jehovah, as the waters cover the sea.

units.leftText: Woe to him who gives drink to his neighbors, pouring it from the wineskin until they are drunk, in order to gaze at their nakedness!
units.rightText: Woe unto him that giveth his neighbor drink, to thee that addest thy venom, and makest him drunken also, that thou mayest look on their nakedness!

units.leftText: You will be filled with shame instead of glory. You too must drink and expose your uncircumcision! The cup in the LORD’s right hand will come around to you, and utter disgrace will cover your glory.
units.rightText: Thou art filled with shame, and not glory: drink thou also, and be as one uncircumcised; the cup of Jehovah’s right hand shall come round unto thee, and foul shame shall be upon thy glory.
leftNotes: 2:16 DSS, LXX, and Syriac and stagger

units.leftText: For your violence against Lebanon will overwhelm you, and the destruction of animals will terrify you, because of your bloodshed against men and your violence against the land, the city, and all their dwellers.
units.rightText: For the violence done to Lebanon shall cover thee, and the destruction of the beasts, which made them afraid; because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all that dwell therein.

units.leftText: What use is an idol, that a craftsman should carve it — or an image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in his own creation; he makes idols that cannot speak.
units.rightText: What profiteth the graven image, that the maker thereof hath graven it; the molten image, even the teacher of lies, that he that fashioneth its form trusteth therein, to make dumb idols?

units.leftText: Woe to him who says to wood, ‘Awake!’ or to silent stone, ‘Arise!’ Can it give guidance? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, yet there is no breath in it at all.”
units.rightText: Woe unto him that saith to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise! Shall this teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in the midst of it.

units.leftText: But the LORD is in His holy temple; let all the earth be silent before Him.
units.rightText: But Jehovah is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.

units.leftText: This is a prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, according to Shigionoth:
units.rightText: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to Shigionoth.
leftNotes: 3:1 Shigionoth is probably a musical term indicating the setting for the prayer.

units.leftText: O LORD, I have heard the report of You; I stand in awe, O LORD, of Your deeds. Revive them in these years; make them known in these years. In Your wrath, remember mercy!
units.rightText: O Jehovah, I have heard the report of thee, and am afraid: O Jehovah, revive thy work in the midst of the years; In the midst of the years make it known; In wrath remember mercy.

units.leftText: God came from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah His glory covered the heavens, and His praise filled the earth.
units.rightText: God came from Teman, And the Holy One from mount Paran. [Selah* His glory covered the heavens, And the earth was full of his praise.
leftNotes: 3:3 Selah or Interlude is probably a musical or literary term; also in verses 9 and 13.

units.leftText: His radiance was like the sunlight; rays flashed from His hand, where His power is hidden.
units.rightText: And his brightness was as the light; He had rays coming forth from his hand; And there was the hiding of his power.

units.leftText: Plague went before Him, and fever followed in His steps.
units.rightText: Before him went the pestilence, And fiery bolts went forth at his feet.

units.leftText: He stood and measured the earth; He looked and startled the nations; the ancient mountains crumbled; the perpetual hills collapsed. His ways are everlasting.
units.rightText: He stood, and measured the earth; He beheld, and drove asunder the nations; And the eternal mountains were scattered; The everlasting hills did bow; His goings were as of old.

units.leftText: I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; the curtains of Midian were trembling.
units.rightText: I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction; The curtains of the land of Midian did tremble.

units.leftText: Were You angry at the rivers, O LORD? Was Your wrath against the streams? Did You rage against the sea when You rode on Your horses, on Your chariots of salvation?
units.rightText: Was Jehovah displeased with the rivers? Was thine anger against the rivers, Or thy wrath against the sea, That thou didst ride upon thy horses, Upon thy chariots of salvation?

units.leftText: You brandished Your bow; You called for many arrows. Selah You split the earth with rivers.
units.rightText: Thy bow was made quite bare; The oaths to the tribes were a sure word. [Selah* Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers.

units.leftText: The mountains saw You and quaked; torrents of water swept by. The deep roared with its voice and lifted its hands on high.
units.rightText: The mountains saw thee, and were afraid; The tempest of waters passed by; The deep uttered its voice, And lifted up its hands on high.

units.leftText: Sun and moon stood still in their places at the flash of Your flying arrows, at the brightness of Your shining spear.
units.rightText: The sun and moon stood still in their habitation, At the light of thine arrows as they went, At the shining of thy glittering spear.

units.leftText: You marched across the earth with fury; You threshed the nations in wrath.
units.rightText: Thou didst march through the land in indignation; Thou didst thresh the nations in anger.

units.leftText: You went forth for the salvation of Your people, to save Your anointed. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked and stripped him from head to toe. Selah
units.rightText: Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people, For the salvation of thine anointed; Thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked man, Laying bare the foundation even unto the neck. [Selah*

units.leftText: With his own spear You pierced his head, when his warriors stormed out to scatter us, gloating as though ready to secretly devour the weak.
units.rightText: Thou didst pierce with his own staves the head of his warriors: They came as a whirlwind to scatter me; Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.

units.leftText: You trampled the sea with Your horses, churning the great waters.
units.rightText: Thou didst tread the sea with thy horses, The heap of mighty waters.

units.leftText: I heard and trembled within; my lips quivered at the sound. Decay entered my bones; I trembled where I stood. Yet I must wait patiently for the day of distress to come upon the people who invade us. Habakkuk Rejoices
units.rightText: I heard, and my body trembled, My lips quivered at the voice; Rottenness entereth into my bones, and I tremble in my place; Because I must wait quietly for the day of trouble, For the coming up of the people that invadeth us.

units.leftText: Though the fig tree does not bud and no fruit is on the vines, though the olive crop fails and the fields produce no food, though the sheep are cut off from the fold and no cattle are in the stalls,
units.rightText: For though the fig-tree shall not flourish, Neither shall fruit be in the vines; The labor of the olive shall fail, And the fields shall yield no food; The flock shall be cut off from the fold, And there shall be no herd in the stalls:

units.leftText: yet I will exult in the LORD; I will rejoice in the God of my salvation!
units.rightText: Yet I will rejoice in Jehovah, I will joy in the God of my salvation.

units.leftText: GOD the Lord is my strength; He makes my feet like those of a deer; He makes me walk upon the heights! For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments.
units.rightText: Jehovah, the Lord, is my strength; And he maketh my feet like hinds’ feet, And will make me to walk upon my high places. For the Chief Musician, on my stringed instruments.
